metadata.generator: text-to-robot design engine (real components + printed structure)
notes: Interpreted locally: type inferred, DOF=8, gripper=parallel.
metadata.source_prompt: Build WALL-E: a tracked trash-compactor robot with a telescoping neck, binocular eyes and two gripper arms

design.summary: Arduino WALL-E: TPU tracks on 4 TT motors, pan/tilt binocular head, 2 servo arms, 0.95 kg, $52 of parts

uses: LM2596 set to 5.0 V for the servos

checks.name: clearance:home
checks.detail: no printed part or component intersects another at the home pose

checks.name: clearance:motion
checks.detail: no interference over 3 combined poses at the joint limits

checks.name: drive:torque
checks.detail: 0.95 kg on a 10 deg slope accelerating 0.5 m/s^2: 0.0210 N·m per wheel vs 0.0235 N·m continuous

checks.name: drive:skid_turn
checks.detail: turning on the spot (mu 1.0, contact 130 mm, track gauge 157 mm): 0.0342 N·m per wheel x 1.3 vs stall 0.0785 N·m (short transient, as for the skid-steer bases)

checks.name: power:servo_supply
checks.detail: four SG90s stalled together draw 2.6 A of the LM2596's 3 A

checks.name: power:driver_current
checks.detail: one TT motor per TB6612FNG channel (stall 1.5 A <= 3.2 A peak)

assumptions: Joint limits trimmed to the collision-free range found by exact solid sweeps: left_arm_lift [-1.00, 1.00] -> [-1.00, 0.35]; right_arm_lift [-1.00, 1.00] -> [-0.35, 1.00].
tracks print in TPU 95A (flexible), everything else in PETG/PLA+; the body prints open side up without supports
TT motor continuous torque taken as 30 % of the 0.8 kg.cm stall; a turn on the spot is a short transient above that (the tracks slide sideways), so spin in bursts on carpet or rubber floors
prices are typical single-unit marketplace prices and vary by seller
